steps.prompt: Think of the last line of a song, a film or a speech you remember. Why do endings stick in our heads?

cards.title: What a closing sentence does
cards.body: A closing sentence wraps up the paragraph. It sums up the main idea in new words and shows why it matters. It doesn’t add a brand-new point.

cards.title: Echo, don’t copy
cards.telling: Topic: Recess should be longer. … Closing: Recess should be longer.
cards.showing: Topic: Recess should be longer. … Closing: For these reasons, an extra fifteen minutes outside would help students learn more inside.
cards.note: Repeat the idea, not the exact words.

cards.title: Three closing moves
cards.text:
Sum up: For these reasons, uniforms are a smart choice.
Show why it matters: Overall, a later start would mean healthier, happier students.
Look ahead: That is why our town should build a skate park before next summer.
cards.note: Avoid a new idea at the end (“Also, uniforms come in many colours.”): it belongs in its own paragraph.

prompts: Read your topic sentence and closing sentence together. How did you say the same idea in new words?
Which closing move (sum up, why it matters, look ahead) do you like best?
